text:
Anya: Quick check-in following yesterday's RFC: can we do live stream handoff on drain instead of forcing reconnects? Idea is zero-visible-hiccup for interactive flows.

Brian: Technically doable but we need a clear handoff contract. Main concerns: KV cache transfer, resume seq numbers, and idempotency.

Devon: We experimented with client-side resume tokens. Pros: simple server model. Cons: client sees a reconnect and some flows break. Also tokens need precise seq semantics to avoid duplicate events.

Celeste: Alternative: node->node delta shipping during drain + a short ownership swap. Client stays connected, proxy routes remain sticky. Adds operational complexity but better UX.

Anya: UX goal: for routes that care (e.g., shell/typing), added tail latency from handoff should be <50ms p95. Otherwise prefer resume reconnect.

Brian: Proposed small proto for orchestration: HandoffOffer(stream_id, origin, target, last_seq, snapshot_uri, timeout_ms). HandoffResponse(stream_id, accepted, applied_seq, checksum). Keep it minimal.

Devon: Sketch of sequence: 1) origin quiesce writes for stream_id; 2) origin produce compact delta (kvcache delta + last_seq); 3) upload delta to internal blobstore or directly stream to target; 4) target validate checksum & warm; 5) atomic lease transfer via coordination service; 6) origin closes local ownership.

Celeste: Observability hooks: handoff.requested, handoff.uploaded, handoff.warmed, handoff.lease_moved, handoff.completed, handoff.fallback. Include trace/span propagation so traces are continuous.

HandoffBot: CI note: edge/handoff-change queued. Integration tests required: graceful-failover, checksum-mismatch, large-snap-fallback.

Brian: Correctness: duplicates and race windows are the killer. Use a short overlap where target accepts but writes only if lease token present. Lease movement must be atomic in coord service (etcd). If lease move fails, target must abort and we fallback to resume-token.

Devon: Performance knobs: cap snapshot_size (default 512KB), cap transfer_ms (default 100ms). If either exceeded, abort and fall back to client-resume. Also rate-limit concurrent handoffs per-node to avoid saturating network.

Anya: Controls: per-route opt-in flag state_handoff, global cluster budget, tenant-level opt-outs. Start with canary: enable for 0.5% of connections and monitor.

Celeste: Metrics to capture: handoff.latency_ms, handoff.failure_rate, handoff.overlap_ms, handoff.snapshot_bytes. Also user-visible signal: client-perceived-reconnect_rate.

Brian: Edge cases: what if target restarts mid-warm? Need idempotent resume on fallback. Also checksum mismatch should surface an alert and increment a repair counter.

Devon: Security: snapshots may contain ephemeral tokens/ids. Ensure snapshots are encrypted in transit and expire (signed URL TTL). Minimal snapshot: only kvcache delta and sequence metadata; no full context.

Anya: Ops runbook: 1) handoff failed -> auto-fallback to resume; 2) if >X% failures in window, auto-disable handoff cluster-wide; 3) run quick reaper to reclaim leases stuck in limbo.

Celeste: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams, the tiny proto, sample snapshot schema, and the Console toggle UX.

Brian: I'll prototype the lease move + checksum check. Also propose a hard cap: snapshot > 1MB => immediate fallback.

Devon: Test plan items: unit proto validation, end-to-end warm handoff under load, chaos (target crash during warm), and perf regression.

Anya: Thanks. If we can keep the fast path simple and opt-in, I'm 👍. Sync tomorrow 11:00 if needed.

HandoffBot: RFC-draft expected by EOD.
